messages:
Maya: quick q — how does /v1/generate handle stop sequences when max_tokens is hit? do we return partial stop fragments, and what do logprobs look like in that case?
Sam: short answer: we return whatever tokens were generated up to the limit. if a stop never fully appears because max_tokens cut it off, the response ends without the stop string. logprobs are included for all emitted tokens.
Maya: ok, that's the behavior i saw in prod but wanted to confirm for the contract tests. also curious about temperature+top_p: if both set by client which takes precedence? any compat guarantees?
Liam: both are supported. implementation note: we scale logits by temperature first, then apply top_p (nucleus) truncation before sampling. that gives reproducible behavior across runtimes. documented in the contract but worth surfacing here.
Ana: two edge cases we ran into in recent fuzz tests: 1) stop sequences that split across token boundaries — tokenization means "\n\n" might be two tokens and stop detection happens on decoded string, not token-aligned. 2) logprobs for the final token are present even if that token completes a stop sequence.
Maya: can you paste an example request/response that shows the partial-stop + logprobs? saves me writing a new test.
Liam: sure — example from the failing runner: 
```json
{"model":"redwood-v1","prompt":"Hello","max_tokens":3,"temperature":0.7,"top_p":0.9,"stop":["end\n"]}
```
Response (conceptual): 
```json
{"text":"This is the e","logprobs":[-1.2,-0.9,-0.5]}
```
Here the stop "end\n" never finished; we returned three tokens and logprobs for all emitted tokens. if a client asserts that returned text must end with a stop string, that'll fail.
Sam: FYI runtime PR #492 adds an explicit note in the spec and makes the contract tests tolerant: either response ends with stop or max_tokens was reached — both valid. i pushed the change, need a CR + CI from eng-ml.
Maya: nice. pinging @Sam for review then. also any caveats about streaming? i noticed when streaming we sometimes send the partial token earlier and then later patch it — how should clients interpret logprobs in streaming mode?
Sam: streaming always emits tokens as they commit; we don't emit logprobs in partial chunks — logprobs are only included on final chunk for a given token. streaming semantics doc updated in the PR.
Ana: one more: older clients omit top_p; defaults remain the same (top_p=1.0). this preserves backward compatibility. if someone sets both and also sets seed, sampling is deterministic with same seed across sessions for the same runtime build.
Maya: thanks — i'll update our contract tests: 1) allow stop-or-max termination, 2) assert logprobs length == tokens returned, 3) verify behavior when stop contains whitespace/token boundaries.
Liam: i added a small unit test in runtime-tests: `test_stop_truncate_logprobs`. Sam, can you add the runtime CI tag so eng-ml tests run on the PR?
Sam: done — added `eng-ml/runtime` label. CI will run on push. :thumbsup:
EvalBot: automatic check: new contract tests found 2 flaky cases related to tokenizer differences across quantized builds. See ticket INF-2134.
Maya: good callout, i'll file a follow-up to relax tokenizer-dependent assertions. thanks all.
Sam: quick heads-up — i'm going to merge the runtime change today after one more review. if anyone needs the exact wording for release notes, I can paste it here.
Maya: please paste the wording, will add to the API changelog.
Sam: "Behavioral note: generation endpoints may terminate due to reaching max_tokens before an explicit stop sequence is emitted. In such cases, the returned text contains all emitted tokens up to the limit and logprobs for each emitted token. When both temperature and top_p are supplied, we apply temperature scaling to logits then perform top_p truncation; sampling proceeds on the resulting distribution. Clients should treat either explicit stop or max_tokens termination as valid contract outcomes."
Maya: perfect. logging this for the tests. thanks everyone.
